name: 16-bit sprite and parallax
summary: Pixel art at 256×224 with up to 256 colours on screen from a 32,768-colour range. Several scrolling layers give parallax depth, sprites carry 15 colours and soft ramps, and skies get gradients made of colour bands.

philosophy.core_thesis: A richer palette and stacked layers let pixel art paint light, air and distance without a 3D engine.
design_principles: Use 2 to 4 background layers that scroll at different speeds for depth.
Shade each sprite with ramps of 3 to 5 steps of one hue, lit from the top left.
Use 15 colours plus transparent in each sprite.
Paint skies as horizontal bands of 4 to 8 colours, not a smooth gradient.
Use selective outlines: dark on the outside, coloured inside.
Make a character 24 to 48 px high.

projection_and_camera.camera: Scrolls with the player; far layers move slower than near layers.
projection_and_camera.framing: 16 by 14 tiles of 16 px; the horizon sits at 40–60% of the height.

geometry.primitive: 8×8 tiles in 2 to 4 layers; sprites up to 64×64.
geometry.budget: 128 sprites, 32 on one line; up to 4 background layers.
geometry.edge_rule: Hard pixel edges, with hand-placed anti-alias pixels on curves.
geometry.proportion: A character is 1.5 to 3 tiles of 16 px; a door is 2 to 3 tiles.

surface.texture_rule: Brick, wood and leaves drawn pixel by pixel with 3- to 5-step ramps.
surface.filtering: Nearest neighbour; sometimes a rotate and scale layer for floors.
surface.material_model: Painted: light and shade are in the pixels.

palette.strategy: Rich, saturated ramps; each layer has its own sub-palettes of 16 colours.
palette.colour_depth: 15 bits for each palette entry, 4 or 8 bits for each pixel

lighting.model: Painted ramps with a fixed light from the top left; colour math for half-transparent layers.
lighting.shadows: Painted cast shadows; a dark oval under each character.
lighting.atmosphere: Colour-band skies, clouds and fog as a half-transparent layer.
lighting.time_of_day: Palette swaps per area: day, dusk and night versions of the same tiles.

world_and_space.scale: Rooms 1 to 2 screens wide; towns several screens with 3 to 6 houses.
world_and_space.interiors: Top-down 3/4 view rooms with visible back and side walls, furniture as sprites.
world_and_space.exteriors: Streets with parallax mountains and clouds behind; house fronts in 3/4 view.
world_and_space.threshold: Walk through a door; fade out and in to the room.

principles.rule: Stack 3 to 4 layers: sky, far land, mid buildings, near ground.
Make a door 1.5 times the height of the character.
Paint 2 light layers: the sky band and warm window light.
Put the warm window light near the player.

interface.placement: Framed boxes in the corners or along the bottom, 10–25% of the screen.
interface.type_and_icons: A pixel font with lower case; small icons of 16 px with outlines.
interface.diegesis: On top; frames are blue gradients or stone borders.

emotion.target_response: A warm, rich nostalgia: the viewer sees a painted world with air in it and wants to explore.

avoid_when: The design must look current and clean.

modifiers.how: Keep the sprites; put them in a 3D diorama with depth of field and real light.
Cut the palette to about 25 colours and drop the parallax.
